clue.text: Risqué adult site — a little memory jogged

indicators.note: something risqué is daring and a bit improper, so the letters before it are taken as being put into a naughty new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: only a little of the word memory is used, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone browsing a racy website finds it brings back a memory or two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Risqué' looks like a description of the website but signals the anagram of ADULTSITE plus M.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory that is jogged has been prompted or roused into action, the sense of excited or prodded.

clue.text: City lifted 8 without frequently booked Belgian

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the pot goes round the turned city

parts.note: the answer to 8 across is a prize such as a cup, which in sporting slang is a pot

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifted means the city's name is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city, is often just Rio

explanation.surface: A city gets hold of a cup, while some Belgian is a regular hotel guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense 'outside'. 'Booked' is the misleading word: it means appearing in many books, not reserving a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's Belgian detective appears in dozens of novels, so he is frequently found in books.

clue.text: Hates playing second — what about 8?

indicators.note: the letters of hates are playing about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: about tells us the exclamation is turned round

parts.note: eh is the questioning exclamation meaning what?

explanation.surface: A cricketer complains about having to bat second and asks about the prize at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges HATES to THEAS; 'about' turns EH into HE. The final question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous England–Australia cricket urn is a prize the two sides compete for, an example of a cup or award.

clue.text: Finally the unalterable is changed — nothing in it for Obama surprisingly

indicators.note: in it puts the zero inside the rearranged letters
the unalterable is changed, so its letters are reshuffled, a joke since unalterable things cannot change

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word the

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Something supposedly fixed has been altered, and Obama, surprisingly, gets nothing from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes E from 'the'; 'is changed' rearranges E plus UNALTERABLE into NBELLAUREATE, and 'in it' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama won the Peace Prize in 2009, early in his presidency, which many found surprising.

clue.text: See 7
Beatle was a little mixed-up in popular 70s film

indicators.note: only slightly muddled: the letters are rearranged, though most stay in place

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Beatle got slightly confused while appearing in a hit film of the seventies.
explanation.walkthrough: The name STARR and WAS share exactly the letters needed; 'a little mixed-up' moves only the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: George Lucas's 1977 space opera was a huge box-office hit and the defining blockbuster of that decade.

clue.text: Rake land with a 4

parts.note: a rake is a womaniser, and as a verb to lech is to behave like one
Wales is a land, one of the countries of the UK

explanation.surface: Someone is told to rake over a piece of land with a tool numbered four.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 refers to the answer at 4 down, a winner of the famous Swedish-funded prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish Solidarity leader received the Peace Prize in 1983, so he is one of its winners.

clue.text: Prize puzzle at first hard — getting nothing at first, go out …

indicators.note: go out means the attempt sits on the outside, wrapping the other letters

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: at first says the zero comes at the front of the inserted group

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word puzzle

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A prize puzzle proves hard at first; getting nowhere, the solver decides to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the sentence on into 9 across and carries no wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup or shield is an award won in competition, a kind of prize.

clue.text: … struggle initially when you get here — time to stop tale of woe

parts.note: your date of birth is when you arrived, and its initials are D, O, B

indicators.note: the time letter is used to stop up, or plug, the jumbled tale
a tale of woe is one in a sorry state, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Continuing from 8 across: a struggle starts on arrival, and it is time to end the sad story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of woe' turns TALE into ATLE, and 'to stop' plugs T into it to make ATTLE. DOB is a form abbreviation for date of birth.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle against someone is to fight them, as two sides do in a battle.

clue.text: Biker's crumpet's unusual attachment to vehicle

indicators.note: unusual letters are out of their normal order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A biker's girlfriend is an odd accessory to be riding on the back of a motorbike.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 's is 'is', a link. 'Crumpet' is British slang for an attractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan sticker is stuck to a car's back fender, a thing attached to a vehicle.

clue.text: Man hurt, forced across country

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: the forcing word stretches across, enclosing, the country

parts.note: made someone do something means forced them
UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A man was injured when made to cross a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a bare definition of a man's name: Marmaduke is an old English given name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an English male first name, as in the cartoon Great Dane, so it is a man.

clue.text: Want to drop daughter where we live

indicators.note: to drop means the daughter letter is let go

parts.note: a dearth is a want or lack
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent longs to leave their daughter at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as a verb, wish, but here is the noun meaning shortage.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet is home to all humans, the place we inhabit.

clue.text: Funeral at last in church — it should bring closure

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word funeral

explanation.surface: A church funeral at last gives the mourners emotional closure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closure' sounds like grief counselling but is literal: the thing shuts a door or gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch on a door or gate fastens it shut, bringing about its closing.

clue.text: Rip sheet up over Emin's unmade bed? Hmm, maybe

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the cloth and the word up are read backwards

parts.note: a pall is a cloth sheet laid over a coffin
taken as the word itself
Tracey Emin's installation My Bed, an unmade bed, was exhibited as art, though some doubted it

explanation.surface: A critic tears into Tracey Emin's notorious unmade-bed artwork and its rumpled sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hmm, maybe' signals the setter's doubt that an unmade bed counts as art. Tracey Emin is a British artist famous for the 1998 work My Bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear something into pieces is to rend or separate it forcibly, the same as ripping.

clue.text: Be frank and address failure

parts.note: to address an audience is to speak or give a talk
a turkey is a flop, especially a failed show or film

explanation.surface: Someone is told to speak openly and deal with their failure.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to discuss something bluntly and plainly, getting down to business.

clue.text: Centre back has United in pocket

indicators.note: has in the sense of holds or contains, so the reversed holiday centre keeps the United letter inside it
back means the holiday centre is read in reverse

parts.note: a resort is a holiday centre
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A football centre-back has a United player in his pocket, marking him closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre back' looks like a football position but splits: 'back' reverses RESORT to TROSER.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket money, especially dubiously, is to take it for yourself, a verb from what you wear.

clue.text: Why English go to food banks? Look up 'Conservative'

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the whole sequence is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the letter Y sounds like the word why
taken as written

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about the English using food banks, with a pointer to a Tory view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up' looks like 'consult' but 'up' reverses Y, E, GO, FD and LO together.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick-in-the-mud who resists change is conservative in the small-c sense, hence the quote marks.

clue.text: Spoon? You listen, weirdo!

parts.note: U is text-speak for you

indicators.note: the weird, odd behaviour signals the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Someone calls another a spoon, a silly fool, and tells the weirdo to listen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoon' is old British slang for a fool, which suits the insult surface. The question mark flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoon is one example of a kitchen implement for eating or cooking.

clue.text: Birds admitting hanky-panky at Queen's like retired academic

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the birds hold the other letters

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
it is slang for sex

explanation.surface: Flightless birds at the palace get up to mischief, rather like a retired don.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex and ER for the Queen are crossword staples.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin title describes a professor who has stood down but keeps the rank as an honour.

clue.text: Music journalist reflected on support — he's honoured

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the music and journalist are read backwards

parts.note: acid house, or acid, is a style of dance music
ED, editor, is the crossword journalist
a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: A music writer looks back on the backing they received and feels honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' reverses ACIDED to DEDICA.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a book or piece is dedicated to is honoured by the dedication.

clue.text: 9 with doctor dressed to go out

indicators.note: the doctor is dressed in the outdoor garment, which wraps round him

parts.note: you put on a coat to go out
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: Someone fights alongside a doctor who is dressed for going outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 is the answer to 9 across, meaning fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight is to engage in a struggle, combat being both noun and verb for this.

clue.text: Artist Max back cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves the opening letters round to the end

parts.note: the stern is the back of a boat

explanation.surface: A painter named Max is back on his bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves ST from the front to the end of STERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German Surrealist and Dada painter, a famous artist.

clue.text: What music maker may do conducting at Eton

indicators.note: conducting means directing the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A composer writes music while conducting at the famous school, Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known private school.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes down melodies in score form, setting them on paper.

clue.text: Attack first — or maybe defend

indicators.note: the words first or maybe defend, or guard, the answer by holding it within them

explanation.surface: A tactical debate: should one attack first or perhaps defend?
explanation.walkthrough: 'defend' looks like the alternative to attack but signals that the answer is held inside 'first or maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack a castle or position is to rush it forcibly, assault it head-on.

clue.text: Cliff and 8 dropping round

indicators.note: dropping means losing the round letter

parts.note: 8 across is a prize, and an Oscar is a film award
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cliff and a prize fall in a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff' might suggest a name, Cliff Richard, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern English place names, a steep rocky outcrop or crag is called by this word.

clue.text: Queen may go here

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, and here is where a cat goes to the toilet indoors

explanation.surface: A royal destination: where Her Majesty might go.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is also a female cat, and 'go' means relieve itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The granules in a tray are where a house cat, including a female one, does its business.

clue.text: Cockney spent some time talking to former Chancellor

indicators.note: talking signals the phrase is spoken aloud and matched by sound

parts.note: a Cockney, dropping his aitches, would say 'ad an 'our for had an hour

explanation.surface: A Londoner passes the time chatting with an ex-head of government.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class East Londoner famous for dropping the H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Konrad was West Germany's first post-war Chancellor, from 1949 to 1963.

clue.text: Lovely girl's quietly entering stage in quest for 8

indicators.note: entering means going inside the girl's word

parts.note: a cutie is an attractive girl
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A pretty girl quietly walks onto a stage while chasing a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' sounds theatrical but means a round of a competition. 8 across is the prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout match in a football cup competition is one round on the way to winning silverware.
